clue.text: Help to present salmon before tea is announced

indicators.note: announced means the phrase is spoken, and its sound is what goes in the grid

parts.note: the coho is a Pacific salmon; put before tea with the 's of 'is' this says 'coho's tea'

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's assistant brings out the salmon just as teatime is called.
explanation.walkthrough: COHO is a kind of Pacific salmon. 'Coho's tea', said aloud as 'announced' asks, runs together into a word for sharing the presenting job.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-host helps another presenter front a show, sharing the role of presenting it.

clue.text: A boatful of students at sea read, wanting a Big Mac …

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up
wanting means lacking, so the word read loses its a

explanation.surface: Students rowing a boat would rather read about a burger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting a' takes the A out of READ, leaving RED, and 'at sea' mixes RED with BIGMAC. The boatful is the Cambridge crew in the Boat Race against Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A university eight that rows in the annual Boat Race on the Thames carries students of that university.

clue.text: … delivered — 100% beef goodness!

indicators.note: delivered as in a speech delivered, so the words are spoken

parts.note: beef made entirely of cow is wholly cow

explanation.surface: Follows on from the Big Mac: the burger arrives, all-beef and delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on the surface of 1 Down; this clue's wordplay stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, mild oaths used in place of stronger ones.

clue.text: Young man attached to second wife has only one small crush

indicators.note: has only one says one of the two letters for small goes

parts.words: Young man attached to second wife
parts.note: a man's second wife may bring a son of her own, his stepson

explanation.surface: A youth with a crush on his stepmother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crush' looks like a youthful infatuation, but it is the verb, to squash.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread on something with your foot is to squash it underfoot.

clue.text: Likely to pass out

definitions.meaning: someone baffled by a quiz question is likely to say 'pass'
in cricket a batsman can be given out this way, by the wicketkeeper breaking the stumps

explanation.surface: Someone woozy and about to faint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass out' reads as fainting, but it splits into two meanings. In cricket, a batsman who leaves the crease can be put out by the wicketkeeper breaking the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: Being baffled makes a quiz contestant pass, and the cricket dismissal is a way of being given out.

clue.text: King overwhelmed with sadness after son blinded

indicators.note: after places the King-and-sadness piece behind the letter for son
overwhelmed with means the word for sadness covers the letter for king

parts.note: woe is sadness
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A king grieves after his son loses his sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blinded' looks like losing sight, but 'to eff and blind' is British slang for swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to blind is to curse, as in 'effing and blinding', so it means cursed.

clue.text: Identification of aggressive man resulted in retreat

indicators.note: retreat means going backwards, so the hidden letters read in reverse
in says the letters sit inside the words aggressive man resulted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Spotting a violent man led to him running away.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'in retreat' to the reversal alone and no word to the hidden step: 'in' is that indicator, 'retreat' the reversal. 'retreat' fits the fleeing aggressor while turning back the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A login name identifies an account holder to a computer system.

clue.text: Stop improving coat with e.g. silver and gold

parts.note: to plate is to coat with a thin layer of metal such as silver
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Advice to stop trying to improve a coat by adding precious metals.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching a level stage after growth means progress stalls and flattens out.

clue.text: Make attractive lady with PhD and energy empty skips

parts.note: a woman with a doctorate is a Dr
E is the symbol for energy in physics

indicators.note: empty means the word skips loses its inside, keeping only its ends

explanation.surface: A drained doctor skips dressing up for the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn or decorate something, a shop window say, makes it look attractive.

clue.text: Woman at university wears hair in curls for a year

indicators.note: the woman wears the curly hairdo, so the hairdo goes around her

parts.note: a perm sets hair in curls
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A student keeps her hair permed for a whole year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means each year, annually, as in a salary quoted yearly.

clue.text: I described 'Piglet' as 'Pit' containing 'leg, originally'

indicators.note: containing says the word for pit holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a pit is a mine

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letter of the word leg

explanation.surface: Seems to be a writer describing a small pig as a hole with a leg in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' is the author talking: A. A. Milne wrote the Winnie-the-Pooh books, in which Piglet appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The creator of Pooh Bear and his small timid pig friend is the author A. A. Milne.

clue.text: Free once, then fixed price

parts.note: ex means former, once
a fixed price is one rate for everybody

explanation.surface: Something that was once free has now been given a set price.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to clear or release them from blame, setting them free of it.

clue.text: Caterer to supply clergyman's office

indicators.note: supply is read as the adverb 'supplely', so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A caterer is hired to provide food for the vicar's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like the verb 'provide', but it is the adverb of supple, meaning flexibly, which signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectorate is the post or term of a rector, a parish priest, so it is his office.

clue.text: Scottish roots, born outside of Prestonpans

parts.note: née, used before a maiden name, means born

indicators.note: outside of asks for the two end letters of Prestonpans

explanation.surface: Someone of Scottish descent who was born outside the town of Prestonpans.
explanation.walkthrough: Prestonpans is a town near Edinburgh, so 'Scottish roots' reads as ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeps is Scots dialect for turnips or swedes, root vegetables served with haggis.

clue.text: Unhappy condition of fox after goose narrowly escaped?

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning glum and dejected

definitions.text: condition of fox after goose narrowly escaped?
definitions.meaning: the fox is left with a mouthful of feathers from the goose

explanation.surface: A fox's gloomy state after its dinner gets away.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is the soft feather of a goose, so a fox that just missed would have it in its jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means depressed or dejected, from the downturned corners of a sad face.

clue.text: See 13
Without men, girls out dancing aren't happy, oddly

indicators.note: dancing means the letters jig about into a new order
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of happy

explanation.surface: Women out dancing without men are not having a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives HPY from 'happy', which 'dancing' mixes with ARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-wedding night out for the bride and her female friends excludes men.

clue.text: Smelly old short trousers where your suit might end up

definitions.text: where your suit might end up

parts.note: meat or game that has gone off is high

indicators.note: trousers is a verb here, meaning pockets, so the word for short takes in the letter for old

parts.note: curt means short

explanation.surface: Reads as old, smelly shorts and where a suit of clothes ends up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing, the same family as 'suit', but is the verb. The suit is a lawsuit, and England's High Court tries big civil cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit may be heard in this senior civil court, so that is where litigation can finish.

clue.text: Tough exterior for one given hard time at grammar school?

definitions.text: Tough exterior for one given hard time at grammar school?

parts.words: Tough exterior for one given hard time at grammar school?
parts.note: a hard-boiled egg is one given a hard time in the pan, and an egghead pupil at a grammar school might have its own private hell

explanation.surface: A bullied clever pupil puts on a hard front.
explanation.walkthrough: A grammar school is a British state secondary school for pupils who pass an exam. The answer splits as 'egg's hell', and a boiled egg is 'given hard time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The brittle casing round an egg is its outer covering, the case kept when one is boiled hard.

clue.text: Mean ginger gent gets recycled present for his girlfriend

indicators.note: recycled means the letters of these three words are reused in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A stingy red-haired man re-gifts something to his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' fits the stingy re-gifting picture but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A man gives his girlfriend this band when proposing, so it is a present for her.

clue.text: Independence cherished by kind of pagan tribe

indicators.note: cherished by means held close by, so the word for kind wraps round the letter

parts.note: a kind person is gentle

explanation.surface: A heathen tribe treasures its freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from Latin gens, clan or nation, and also describes heathens or non-Jews.

clue.text: See 18
It expanded what was written by Dante, among others

definitions.meaning: It. is the short form of the word, so expanding the abbreviation gives the full word

definitions.text: what was written by Dante, among others
definitions.meaning: the language Dante wrote the Divine Comedy in

explanation.surface: Something grew larger and Dante wrote about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun, but it is the abbreviation It., also familiar as Italian vermouth in 'gin and it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante, Petrarch and Boccaccio composed their works in the language of Italy.

clue.text: Dead gorgeous actress bleating about calories put on two pounds

indicators.note: in a down clue put on means placed on top of what follows
about means the bleat goes around the letter for calories

parts.note: baa is the bleating of a sheep
C is the abbreviation for calories
L is the abbreviation for pound, so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: A stunning actress complains about calories after gaining two pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead gorgeous' is British slang for very attractive, but here 'dead' is literal: Lauren Bacall died in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauren Bacall was a glamorous Hollywood film star of the 1940s, now deceased.

clue.text: Forbid these to stop partners wishing to make contract

definitions.text: Forbid these to stop partners wishing to make contract

parts.note: forbid means ban
in bridge North and South are partners

explanation.surface: Objectors try to block a couple who want to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbid the banns' is the old phrase for objecting to a wedding when the banns are read. Bridge partners North and South also bid to 'make contract'.
explanation.definitionFit: Banns are the church announcement of a coming marriage, at which anyone may raise an objection.

clue.text: Couch potato carrying wife around for sociable sport

indicators.note: carrying means the turned-round word holds the letter for wife
around means the word for couch potato is turned round

parts.note: a couch potato is a slob

explanation.surface: A lazy man carries his wife about for a sociable pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns SLOB into BOLS, and 'carrying' puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn bowling on a green is a gentle game known for its friendly club atmosphere.

clue.text: Is missing Saudi boarding stylish coach?

indicators.note: Is is read as two letter I's, which are left out
boarding means getting on, so the Saudi goes inside the word for stylish

parts.note: stylish means chic
a Saudi is an Arabian

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Saudi boarding a smart coach has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the verb, but it is read as the plural of the letter I: both I's go, one from each piece once the Saudi has boarded.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned motor coach used for outings and day trips.

clue.text: Shock given by cold dentist's equipment

indicators.note: given by puts the letter for cold before the word for shock

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, on taps
a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: A cold dentist's tools give a patient a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like a fright, but it is a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Patients sit in a reclining seat at the dentist's, part of the surgery's equipment.

clue.text: I wait quaking with 'Beth Fry

indicators.note: quaking means shaking, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone trembles while waiting with Beth, a woman called Fry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fry' looks like a surname, or cooking, but it means young fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitebait are the young of herring and sprat, so they are fry, tiny fish.

clue.text: "I'll be seeing you every so often," said nice guy

indicators.note: every so often picks out every other letter of said nice guy, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A nice guy promises to drop by now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every so often' looks like part of the quoted farewell, but it is the instruction to take alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying goodbye; the French word is a farewell.

clue.text: Sunny maybe found among lost Ella recordings

indicators.note: found among says the letters sit inside the words lost Ella recordings

explanation.surface: A cheerful song turns up among missing Ella Fitzgerald tapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunny' looks like a song title, but it means 'of the sun', and the Sun is a star.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a star, so anything belonging to it is to do with stars.

clue.text: Plot alien object in orbit

parts.note: a plot is a plan
ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: A scheme to send a strange object into orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars or Venus travels around the Sun, an example of a body circling a star.
